0.content: Adorno was Captain of the 5th Company, a veteran of Varka's campaigns, and in later years a semi-retired fixture of Dornman Port who handed out candy and rescued lost cats. Leading a rescue with blunt arrows, he freed the children Eroch's men had abducted, Lohen among them. The rescue earned him the title "Benevolent Knight", though he felt he never deserved it because he had failed to find the experiment site or ease Lohen's trauma. He guided Lohen from the Adventurers' Guild into the Knights. He recommended him for the Nod-Krai expedition on condition that Lohen reflect on what makes a virtuous knight and then inherit his title and captaincy.

1.content: Theodore was kidnapped with Lohen as a child; Lohen remembers him as the "goof" who would not stop crying. He failed the knight exams, became a trainee medic of the 8th Company, and cared for the ageing Adorno. Recalling Eroch's lab from childhood, he restarted the Ursa experiments to make a life-prolonging serum. Lohen, who had read Theodore's health report on Adorno, cleaned up his escaped test subjects. He kept the secret and offered himself as a test subject because he wanted the power.

2.content: Lohen came to the Knights already hunting Varka. Varka was the "living legend" who had driven Eroch to his death. As a recruit, Lohen ambushed him with arrows, smoke, traps and sedatives. Varka subdued him, confined him for a few days and told him to try again whenever he liked. Lohen came back with a bottle of Varka's favourite Dandelion Wine, heavily drugged; Varka shrugged off the dizziness by sheer will. The lesson stuck: real strength is the kind no trap or poison can shake.

3.content: Riding in his father's cargo wagon to deliver bows to Mondstadt, the young Lohen was taken by masked men in black robes. Skilled bandits had drawn his father away first, and the father, used to a quiet life, never fought back. In a cell with other crying children, Lohen hid an arrowhead in his sleeve and had nicked his ropes by the time Adorno's knights intercepted the transport. The plot belonged to Eroch, the Knights' Inspector, who was experimenting with one of Dottore's Segments on serum drawn from Ursa the Drake's flesh.

4.comment: Lohen: A Knight's Legacy and Ursa's flesh
4.content: Lohen's story quest (6.6). Due to receive a title and the 5th Company captaincy at the expedition's award ceremony, Lohen took the Traveler to see Adorno. In a test of Sucrose's Simulation Training Bubble, a memory of Rerir set him off and he released an unfamiliar power. Ursa-tainted monsters were roaming near Dornman Port. Varka and Diluc learned that Theodore had restarted Eroch's experiments and that Lohen had joined him.

5.content: On the Nod-Krai expedition Lohen barely visited the Favonius Keep, spending his time hunting the Wild Hunt in the wilds. With Varka he ambushed Rerir, the Rächer of Solnari, was badly beaten and spent days in camp. By the time he could stand, the Traveler and their allies had banished Rerir. Then he and part of the 5th Company were sent home, so he also missed the fight with Dottore.

6.content: The Knights of Favonius' ranged company: crossbowmen and musketeers who split into squads to support other companies. Lohen calls it an ordinary ranged support team. Under Lohen its tactics changed: he charges ahead with a spear as both shield and bait, so his squads fire at will. The expedition came to know him as its "Frontline Suppression Officer". Mika says its members are always on standby for the thick of the action and that Lohen inspires them to follow his reckless tactics.

7.content: Mika, a surveyor close to Lohen's age, was flattered when the "notorious" senior praised his surveying device and asked about it. He then noticed that every area Lohen asked about went quiet within days, and that Lohen kept coming back with fresh cuts. He started leaving monster camps off the maps. Lohen says one look at Mika's face was enough to find them anyway.

8.comment: Lohen: The Traveler and the friendship fee
8.content: Lohen met the Traveler at the Thousand Winds Temple in 6.4, while delivering Varka's letters. In 6.6 he paid them a 100,000-Mora "friendship fee", drawn from his unspent special-mission allowance, to pose as his friends before Adorno. He promised not to tell a single lie, and he didn't, though he narrated his methods "with some delicacy". By the end of the quest he trusted them to fight Ursa while he held the monsters, and Varka remarked that the fee had not been a complete waste after all.
